episodes.180327: Extreme instability developed during the day which lead to widespread thunderstorm development in an environment with little to no winds aloft.
episodes.180349: An upper level trough tracked across the Northern Rockies, dragging its base across the Western Slope. This resulted in increased instability and moisture which fueled scattered showers and thunderstorms. Convection was high-based given the abundance of dry air at the lower levels. Even so, a stronger storm in northeast Utah produced quarter-sized hail near Maeser.
episodes.180368: Thunderstorms produced heavy rain in Orangeburg which led to some flash flooding.
episodes.180475: A backdoor front entered northeastern NM during the early morning hours increasing surface moisture across the region. This added moisture along with daytime heating allowed isolated supercells to develop across southeastern Colfax and eastern Mora counties, moving southeast towards the Texas state line. Storms produced up to golf ball sized hail in Springer and near Roy, and wind gusts of up to 74 mph at Tucumcari.
episodes.180508: A severe thunderstorm flipped over planes at the Kissimmee Gateway Airport.
episodes.180698: A weak upper trough lingered from the Ohio Valley southwest into the Mid-South region and Southern Arkansas on July 5th, as it was blocked between upper ridges centered to the west and east over the Southern Rockies and West Texas, and over the Gulf Coast states. Strong heating within a moist air mass resulted in strong instability developing during the afternoon, with large scale forcing ahead of the trough adequate enough for the development of widely scattered showers and thunderstorms across portions of Southern Arkansas. One isolated severe thunderstorm developed over El Dorado in Union County Arkansas, with several trees blown down across the city and a church sign damaged from the damaging winds.
episodes.180819: Showers and thunderstorms were moving slowly due to little wind aloft. This led to some flash flooding in northern Virginia.
episodes.181417: A poorly organized complex of thunderstorms crossed southeast Missouri during the peak heating hours late in the afternoon. An isolated occurrence of wind damage was reported in one of the strongest cells. The storms occurred along a cold front that trailed southwest from a low pressure center over Lake Michigan.
episodes.181418: A small, isolated thunderstorm cell produced damaging winds over a very small area in Hopkinsville. The storm occurred in hot, unstable air ahead of a cold front over southeast Missouri.
episodes.181489: Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms developed over southern WI with the passage of weak low pressure and a cold front. Mostly tree damage was observed. Street flooding occurred in Milwaukee after a couple slow moving thunderstorms affected the area.
episodes.181619: Showers and thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon over the central/eastern Piedmont and central Coastal Plain. The storms then drifted southward over the Sandhills and southern Piedmont by the evening and overnight.
episodes.181647: Numerous thunderstorms developed over southern Wisconsin and tracked over the nearshore and open waters of Lake Michigan.
episodes.181706: Sea breeze storms over a very moist and unstable airmass produced localized strong to severe wind gusts.
episodes.181867: An isolated thunderstorm resulted in a downburst causing localized wind damage over a small portion of Fairfax County, Virginia.
episodes.181923: Widespread severe weather was observed across Eastern Nebraska on the afternoon and evening of July 4. Storms initially were discrete or multi-clustered and produced mainly hail. The largest hail report was 2.75 inches near Tarnov in Platte County. A QLCS formed as storms merged along a cold front and strong wind gusts became the primary hazard. Numerous locations observed 60+ mph wind gusts. An estimated peak wind gust of 80 mph caused damage to trees and power poles near Weston.
episodes.182056: A slow-moving cold front resulted in clusters of thunderstorms developing across central Illinois during the afternoon. These storms eventually merged into a line as they moved into eastern Illinois during the early evening. These storms resulted in a few instances of wind damage.
episodes.182082: The combination of an upper-level disturbance and nearby surface low and frontal boundary resulted in isolated showers and thunderstorms across portions of eastern New York on July 4, 2023. A few of these thunderstorms became severe producing downed trees and wires. A more concentrated area of damage occurred from the Rensselaer/Columbia County line southward to Styvesant. A NWS Storm Survey confirmed a straight line wind event occurred with winds estimated up to 100 mph causing widespread damage.
episodes.182109: An upper level trough was over the northern Rocky Mountains and Northern Plains and was bringing a cold front south through Nebraska during the afternoon and evening hours of Independence Day. Temperatures heated up in advance of the front with dewpoints mostly in the 60s. A very moist and unstable atmosphere was present. CAPE values were generally near 4,000 J/kg ahead of the front, and 0 to 6 km wind shear values were around 35 knots. Mid-level lapse rates were generally 7 to 8 degrees C/km. ||Isolated showers and storms were moving across portions of south central Nebraska during the early to mid-afternoon hours. This activity did not produce any severe weather. The main storm activity developed late in the afternoon into the evening hours and was associated with the cold front moving through Nebraska. Storms began developing in central Nebraska in the late afternoon and early evening hours. Then storms developed in south central Nebraska and formed a line with the storms in the central part of the state. The storms in central Nebraska moved southeast during the evening hours while the storms in the south central part of the state remained fairly stationary. The storms produced large hail and wind gusts of 58 to 66 mph between 5:30 PM CDT and 9 PM CDT. The largest hail reported was up to 2.50 inches and was reported in Webster, Fillmore, and Thayer Counties.
episodes.182110: An upper level trough was over the northern Rocky Mountains and Northern Plains and was bringing a cold front south into Kansas during the early evening hours of Independence Day. Temperatures heated up in advance of the front with dewpoints mostly in the 60s. A very moist and unstable atmosphere was present. CAPE values were generally near 4,000 J/kg ahead of the front, and 0 to 6 km wind shear values were around 35 knots. Mid-level lapse rates were generally 7 to 8 degrees C/km.||A storm developed and produced golf ball sized hail in Smith County in north central Kansas at 4:45 PM CDT. This was the biggest hail of the day in north central Kansas. This storm continued to grow in size and then split apart with one part of the storm moving to the west and the other part moving to the east. The east moving storm began moving southeast and formed into a bowing structure. This storm produced winds ranging from 58 mph to 71 mph in Phillips and Osborne Counties. The severe reports ended with a 68 mph wind gust in Phillips County just before 8 PM CDT.
episodes.182249: On July 4, showers and thunderstorms developed across most of the state around noon.  The line of storms across southern New Hampshire contained localized downpours that dropped 2 to 3��� over a 3 hour period in Stoddard and Wolfeboro.  Additional flooding was reported in both of these towns during the early afternoon hours with road flooding and erosion damage being reported.  Across northern New Hampshire isolated thunderstorm downpours were estimated to drop up to 2��� in an hour in the rural mountains of Coos County and near Mount Moosilauke in the White Mountains National Forest.  Heavy rain showers and thunderstorms were isolated into the evening hours in the Connecticut River Valley but no additional flooding was reported in these areas.  In addition, a few isolated storms around the state become severe with sporadic tree damage due to wind damage, along with a few reports of low end severe hail.
episodes.182985: Scattered thunderstorms developed and moved through parts of Eastern NC during the late afternoon hours. A couple storms became severe and produced damaging winds.
episodes.182986: Slow moving thunderstorms produced very heavy rain and some flash flooding in the Jacksonville area, as well as around Wallace.
episodes.182996: A typical summer pattern persisted with scattered thunderstorms across the area with a few reports of severe weather.
episodes.183024: A strong dust devil that developed in Apache Junction caused impacts to a mobile home park, damaging car ports and rolling over storage sheds.
episodes.183061: Several rounds of thunderstorms impacted the combined OK/TX Panhandles during the early evening hours of the 5th and going through into the early AM hours of the 6th. First, in the eastern TX Panhandle. Then a complex came in from eastern New Mexico impacting the southwestern TX Panhandle. Another complex then came in from SE Colorado and SW Kansas impacting the northern combined OK/TX Panhandles. Severe winds occurred with these storms and one instance of 1 hail also occurred. The strongest winds were with the complex that came into the OK Panhandle with winds upwards of 70 to 80 mph. The storms that started out early in the eastern TX Panhandle produced some heavy rainfall as well, as these storms moved slowly and eventually merged into one large storm moving south through the rest of the eastern TX Panhandle.
episodes.183127: Diurnally-driven strong to marginally severe thunderstorms developed during peak heating. Localized wind damage and heavy rain were the main hazards.
episodes.183252: Mother Nature supplied most of the fireworks for the Fourth of July as severe thunderstorms moved across the region during the late afternoon and evening.  Intense wind gusts, locally heavy rain and minor street flooding accompanied the storms.  Denver Fire performed a swift water rescue in the area of 38th Avenue and Fox Street, in the evening when a motorist became stranded in their vehicle.  Several fireworks shows were either cancelled or postponed due to safety concerns associated with the inclement weather.  Peak wind gusts included:  74 mph northwest of Red Feather Lakes, 70 mph just northeast of Kremmling, and 67 mph at Buckley AFB.  Several areas along the urban corridor picked up anywhere from 1 to 2 inches of rainfall.  At Denver International Airport, a storm produced 0.77 inch of rainfall along with a peak wind gust to 54 mph.
episodes.183296: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along and south of I-40 due to diurnal heating during the late afternoon on July 4, 2023. Weak wind shear combined with deep moisture produced slow-moving, highly efficient rainfall-producing thunderstorms. There were several reports of flash flooding across the area.
episodes.183297: Scattered showers and thunderstorms developed along and south of I-40 due to diurnal heating during the late afternoon on July 4, 2023. Weak wind shear combined with deep moisture produced slow-moving, highly efficient rainfall-producing thunderstorms. There were several reports of flash flooding across the area.
episodes.183301: A cold front pushed into the Mid-South during the afternoon and evening hours on July 5, 2023. The front interacted with an unstable airmass favorable for producing strong downdrafts. Numerous showers and thunderstorms developed along the front as it moved into areas along and north of I-40. A few of the storms produced damaging winds.
episodes.183344: In early July there were significant reports of hail, damaging wind, and flash flooding. The month got off to a quick start with golf ball size hail just east of Omaha (Boone County) on the 1st. On the 5th, there was a 62 mph wind gust measured at Newport (Jackson County).
episodes.183345: An upper level low crossed the region during the 5th. Instability due to diurnal heating and the cold pool aloft supported the development of thunderstorms during the afternoon. Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms occurred across portions of Downeast Maine with hail and damaging winds.
episodes.183511: Scattered strong to severe thunderstorms were seen throughout western Illinois. One storm produced strong outflow winds, which led to some tree damage in Elizabeth, Illinois.
episodes.183530: An isolated strong to severe storm produce localized damaging winds.
episodes.183630: Clusters of strong thunderstorms developed across southeast Georgia during the afternoon hours. These thunderstorms eventually tracked to the coast and produced strong wind gusts into the early evening hours.
episodes.183711: A thunderstorm created strong winds across Kearny County.
episodes.183852: Return flow and afternoon instability prompted a couple of isolated storms across eastern Kentucky during the evening hours on July 5th. One of these storms resulted in a damaging wind which took down a tree and powerlines in Perry County.
episodes.183884: A squall line quickly developed late in July 4th and produced widespread wind damage across the CWA. Winds exceeded 80 mph at times.
episodes.184056: A mid atmospheric disturbance moved over a unstable airmass across northern Vermont during the afternoon hours of July 4th. Scattered thunderstorms rotated north to southeast across the region, some of them providing localized damaging winds.
episodes.184094: A weak trough of 500 MB low pressure helped trigger locally heavy rains over western portions of the Tennessee Valley.
episodes.184126: Residual moisture from an incredibly anomalously wet June continues to moisten the lower levels aiding in ample amounts of instability. The northwest flow pattern created a lot of shear, which led to prolonged 3 day severe weather event over adjacent and eastern plains of southern Colorado.
episodes.184224: A cluster of strong thunderstorms brought damaging winds, torrential rainfall, and flash flooding to parts of northern Illinois during the afternoon and evening of July 5. Several rain gauges around the area recorded one to two inches of rain within a 30 minute period underneath some of these storms. The city of Chicago and its near-south and near-west suburbs were the areas hit hardest. Numerous reports were received of flooded roads, including a number of residential streets. Additionally, two firefighters were injured battling a fire caused by lightning striking a townhouse.
episodes.184268: Scattered storms developed each afternoon hours and a few became strong to severe which downed some trees.
episodes.184280: Storms developed along an old outflow boundary over portions of southwest Illinois. Some of the storms became strong to severe with damaging winds reported.
episodes.184335: A large complex of thunderstorms moved across northern Kansas into central Kansas and southeast Kansas during the evening hours of July 4th, 2023.  The line of thunderstorms produced damaging wind reports and a few large hail reports. The complex of storms also brought heavy rainfall to some areas.
episodes.184590: A southwest to northeast corridor of storm activity occurred during the afternoon through early evening across Northwest Kansas.  The largest hail reported from these storms was near Tasco.  The dry, loose ground, combined with the thunderstorms winds produced near zero visibility near Monument and Selkirk.  Wind gusts up to an estimated 90 MPH near Norton blew the roof off of a cabin.  Lastly, a landspout occurred along the west edge of the thunderstorm activity north of Tribune.
episodes.186194: A cluster of strong thunderstorms brought torrential rainfall and gusty winds over southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon and evening of the 5th.
